sources.title: GPT-5.3 Instant: Smoother, more useful everyday conversations
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The March 3 announcement explicitly binds GPT-5.3 Instant to gpt-5.3-chat-latest. It reports conversation, web-search and factuality improvements but no nominal total or active parameter count. Its sample-response use of the word parameters concerns an archery problem, not model size.

sources.title: GPT-5.3 Chat model documentation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Exact API page and freshly fetched Markdown identify GPT-5.3 Chat as the GPT-5.3 Instant snapshot, now shut down. They document text/image input, text output, 128,000-token context, 16,384 output tokens, Chat Completions, Responses and function calling. Markdown additionally lists a conflicting 272,000 maximum input tokens. Neither publishes model parameter counts or a counted base-model relationship.

sources.title: GPT-5.3 Instant System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026; read the complete five-page original PDF. March 3 card names GPT-5.3 Instant and gpt-5.3-instant equivalently. Section 2 describes training data and a February 26 evaluated version; Tables 1-3 report safety/HealthBench scores and response length. No nominal total, activated count or named base with a published size is specified.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 Instant System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026; checked the complete 21-page May 4 PDF and exact GPT-5.3 Instant comparison tables. The introduction identifies GPT-5.3 Instant as the baseline; Tables 1-6 and later preparedness comparisons report evaluation metrics, not total or active parameters. Full-text count searches found no numerical parameter disclosure or usable size lineage for GPT-5.3 Instant.

sources.title: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. May 7 training research covers GPT-5.1 Instant through GPT-5.4 Instant and GPT-5.2 Instant through GPT-5.4 Instant, including GPT-5.3 Instant. It discusses accidental chain-of-thought grading, limited CoT and affected training-sample fractions, but supplies no nominal model count or explicit counted-base relationship.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses supports PDF input; vision-capable models receive extracted text and page images. Chat Completions also accepts PDFs. Combined with the exact model vision and endpoint support, this establishes PDF as an API input format, not an additional native modality.

sources.title: Deprecations
sources.evidence: The May 8, 2026 notice explicitly lists gpt-5.3-chat-latest with API shutdown on August 10, 2026.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: March 3, 2026 entry releases the exact API ID to Chat Completions and Responses. March 16 entry explicitly updates the same slug to the latest ChatGPT model, establishing mutable alias behavior.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: The service agreement grants limited nonexclusive API/service access in section 2.2 and reserves service intellectual-property ownership in section 9.1. This supports a descriptive proprietary service classification, not a downloadable-weight license.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6 and explains Transformer attention key/value projections and caching. It provides a mechanism, but no exact GPT-5.3 Chat binding; the model cached-input price alone is insufficient to establish structural architecture.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Current guide explains KV storage and separates pre-5.6 behavior. Its explicit extended-retention list does not name gpt-5.3-chat-latest. Generic earlier-model descriptions do not independently establish this exact variant architecture.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 Instant: smarter, clearer, and more personalized
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. May 5 announcement replaces GPT-5.3 Instant with GPT-5.5 Instant as the ChatGPT default and compares behavior, factuality and response style. It supplies no total or activated parameter counts for GPT-5.3 Instant. The paid-user legacy-access schedule is separate from the API shutdown notice.

sources.title: GPT-5.3 Instant System Card web page
sources.evidence: HTML page header says March 2, whereas its PDF cover and explicit public launch are March 3. The card also references a February 26 evaluated version; those dates are recorded without overriding the explicit API launch.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-5.3 Chat record
sources.evidence: Original catalog lead was inspected; it asserts reasoning=false and generic gpt family. Those assertions are checked independently against primary release, API and training evidence rather than treated as proof.

sources.title: GPT-5.3 Chat model documentation, Markdown
sources.evidence: Fetched October 27, 2026 (HTTP 200) and read in full. The exact gpt-5.3-chat-latest model specification identifies the GPT-5.3 Instant snapshot and lists token limits, modalities, prices and API features. It has no total or active parameter specification; token limits and rate limits are not model-size evidence.

name.note: Use the official API display name; latest remains in the API identifier.

developer.note: Developer identified by its own announcement and system card.

family.note: Normalize the explicitly named GPT-5.3 variant to gpt-5.3; do not merge it with Codex or another Instant generation.

release_date.note: Explicit public API launch controls. February 26 is a card version date, March 2 an HTML publication label, and March 16 an alias update; none establishes an earlier public API release.

open_weights.note: Released through hosted ChatGPT/API services under reserved service IP; no downloadable-weight release identified in the checked first-party material.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-service licensing classification, not SPDX or an open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit reopened the original release/card and current exact API specification, then checked the later GPT-5.5 Instant release/card and training research. No nominal total or explicit lineage to a base with a published count was found. Bounded fresh first-party and exact-model research searches found no later numerical disclosure; the unresolved count is not a demand for a tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit checked active parameters separately. Exact-model columns in the later GPT-5.5 Instant card are evaluation scores, not activated-parameter counts; targeted searches for explicit active/activated comparison tables found no usable original model-team source for GPT-5.3 Instant. No active count or counting convention is established, and none is inferred from the family or a dense assumption.

architecture.note: Original/later cards and targeted first-party architecture, training and interpretability searches did not establish exact structural details. Pre-5.6 KV explanation lacks an exact-variant binding beyond cached pricing; do not infer Transformer or dense/MoE structure from that alone.

context_window.note: Retain the explicit context-window value shown in HTML and Markdown. The separate 272,000 maximum-input line conflicts; no larger capacity is inferred. These are last-documented limits, not a live endpoint test.

modalities.note: Native text/image input and text output; PDF is included as the API-supported document format processed into text and page images. No native audio/video support is established.

reasoning.note: The exact Instant-to-API binding and research ranges including GPT-5.3 establish limited internal CoT. This corrects false without claiming user-selectable reasoning effort, full Thinking-model behavior or access to raw CoT.

tool_call.note: The exact variant explicitly supports function calling; no capability is transferred from another GPT-5.3 model.

patch.notes: Mutable alias for GPT-5.3 Instant: launched March 3, 2026 and updated March 16. The system card evaluates a February 26 version; its HTML March 2 label differs from the March 3 PDF and public launch. OpenAI lists API shutdown on August 10, 2026; ChatGPT replacement and legacy access followed a separate May 5 announcement. Technical fields describe documented capabilities, not current endpoint availability. Reasoning means limited internal chain of thought, not an exposed effort control. PDF is an API input format converted to text and images. Context remains 128,000; a conflicting 272,000 maximum-input line is not adopted. Total and active parameter counts are undisclosed in the checked original specifications and later exact-model comparisons; no counted-base lineage is established. Structural architecture remains unverified.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter-only re-audit retained undisclosed total and active counts after reopening the original GPT-5.3 Instant sources, current exact API specification, later GPT-5.5 Instant comparisons and OpenAI training research. Fresh targeted disclosure and activated-parameter-table searches found no supported nominal count or counted-base lineage. Added explicit null parameter patches and refreshed evidence; preserved the other twelve assessments.
